question.worked_solution:
Squaring both sides of the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2-3x} & =2 \\ {(\sqrt{2-3x})}^{2} & ={2}^{2} \\ 2-3x & =4 \\ 3x & =-2 \\ x & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's check the result by plugging it into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2-3(-\frac{2}{3})} & \overset{?}{=}2 \\ \sqrt{2-\cancel{3}(-\frac{2}{\cancel{3}})} & \overset{?}{=}2 \\ \sqrt{2-(-2)} & \overset{?}{=}2 \\ \sqrt{2+2} & \overset{?}{=}2 \\ \sqrt{4} & \overset{?}{=}2 \\ 2 & =2\,\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

The value $x=-\frac{2}{3}$ satisfies the original equation, so we can accept it as a solution.

Therefore, the solution to $\sqrt{2-3x}=2$  is $x=-\frac{2}{3}.$
